invariants.rationale: The method returns item.toString(), so the result must equal item.toString().
item.toString() in Java never returns null, so result is guaranteed non-null.
item.toString() would throw NullPointerException if item was null, so item must be non-null by the point of return.
Since result equals item.toString(), their lengths must match.
item.toString() returns a String, so result is always a String object.
